title: AlgebrasTQD: Computing Algebras and Interfaces in Twisted Quantum Doubles
abstract: We present AlgebrasTQD, an open-source code written in GAP (Groups, Algorithms, and Programming), for computing condensable algebras and the corresponding topological boundaries and interfaces of twisted quantum doubles $D^ω(G)$. These algebras can be used to classify 1+1d gapped and gapless phases whose symmetry is related by gauging to a finite group $G$ with anomaly $ω\in H^3(G,U(1))$, to study 2+1d anyon proliferation and to construct logical gates in non-Abelian topological quantum codes. The functions in AlgebrasTQD compute all condensable algebras $A(H,F,γ,ε)$ with their algebra structure and anyons, sort them into isomorphism classes and identify the twin algebras that are inequivalent but share the same anyon decomposition. AlgebrasTQD also determines all the subalgebra relations, the corresponding Hasse diagram and the types of 1+1d phases for any chosen, possibly non-invertible, group-theoretical symmetry. For non-maximal algebras, the code computes the reduced topological order with its $3$-cocycle and the map of anyons across the topological interface. Finally, AlgebrasTQD includes functions that construct certain non-Clifford logical gates via non-Abelian surface codes. We summarize the formulas that are implemented in the AlgebrasTQD code, and we illustrate its use with Abelian and non-Abelian groups including $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ with $ω_\text{III}$, $D_8$, $A_4$ with and without anomaly, twin algebras and twin phases, and the Clifford-hierarchy gates in quantum doubles of dihedral groups. All arithmetic is exact and AlgebrasTQD can be used with any finite group $G$ and 3-cocycle $ω$, limited only by the time and size of the calculation. The code is available at https://github.com/AlisonWarman/AlgebrasTQD
summary: This paper presents AlgebrasTQD, a computational tool for analyzing condensable algebras associated with twisted quantum doubles $D_\omega(G)$. It allows for the rigorous classification of 1+1d topological phases by computing the algebra structure, identifying equivalent/inequivalent phases, and determining the nature of topological interfaces. This is vital for understanding exotic quantum matter and designing quantum error-correcting codes.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computation and classification of condensable algebras and their corresponding topological boundaries and interfaces for twisted quantum doubles $D_\omega(G)$. This is crucial for understanding symmetry-protected topological phases in 1+1d systems.
main_result: The authors introduce AlgebrasTQD, an open-source code that computes the full structure of these algebras, classifies them into isomorphism classes, and identifies twin algebras, thereby advancing the classification of gapped and gapless phases.
method: The methodology relies on advanced group theory and algebraic computation implemented in the GAP software package to analyze the structure of condensable algebras $A(H, F, \gamma, \epsilon)$.
model_or_system: The theoretical framework centers on Symmetry Topological Field Theories (SymTFT) realized via twisted quantum doubles $D_\omega(G)$. These models are used to study 2+1d anyon proliferation and construct logical gates in non-Abelian topological quantum codes.
key_observables: Condensable algebras, anyon types, topological boundaries, interfaces, and the resulting classification of 1+1d gapped/gapless phases.
important_parameters: The finite group $G$ and the anomaly $\omega \in H^3(G, U(1))$ are the primary input parameters, with the code being general for any such pair.
main_assumptions: The primary limitation noted is computational time and size, but the code is claimed to be exact for any finite group $G$ and 3-cocycle $\omega$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the SymTFT slab, showing the relationship between the symmetry fixing boundary ($L_{sym}$), the physical boundary ($A_{phys}$), and the interface to a reduced topological order. Figure 2 shows the modular S matrix.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of computing condensable algebras for $D_\omega(G)$, details the functionality of the AlgebrasTQD code (including functions for subgroups, cocycles, and algebra structure), presents the mathematical framework for classifying phases and interfaces, and concludes with applications to non-Clifford logical gates.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general computational tool for classifying complex topological phases that arise in condensed matter systems, connecting abstract algebra to physical observables like anyon statistics and phase transitions.
